questions.question: The transportation mechanism in cells by which food or other useful molecules from the outside are carried inside the cell is known as ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endocytosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Endocytosis** is a cellular process in which substances are brought into the cell.
 
• It involves the cell membrane folding around the desired molecules to form a vesicle that is brought into the cell.
 
• Endocytosis is crucial for the intake of nutrients and other essential molecules that cannot pass through the cell membrane by diffusion.
 
• There are different types of endocytosis, including phagocytosis (ingestion of large particles) and pinocytosis (ingestion of fluids and small molecules).
 
• Endocytosis plays a significant role in cellular signaling, nutrient uptake, and immune responses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exocytosis** is the process by which cells expel materials in vesicles by fusing them with the cell membrane.
 
• **Osmosis** refers to the movement of water molecules through a semi-permeable membrane from a region of low solute concentration to high solute concentration.
 
• **Diffusion** is the passive movement of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration.
 
• **Phagocytosis** is a type of endocytosis where the cell engulfs large particles or even whole cells, typically seen in immune cells like macrophages.
 
• **Pinocytosis** is another type of endocytosis where the cell engulfs extracellular fluid and dissolved solutes, often referred to as "cell drinking."

questions.question: ________ are a kind of waste disposal system of the cell.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosomes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes**:-

 
 
• These are small, spherical organelles that contain digestive enzymes.
 
• They are responsible for breaking down a wide variety of cellular waste products, including worn-out organelles, food particles, and bacteria.
 
• Lysosomes are also involved in recycling cellular components, such as amino acids and proteins. 
 
• **Lysosomes are a kind of waste disposal system of the cell.**
 
• Lysosomes are essential for maintaining cell health and function.
 
• If lysosomes are not functioning properly, cellular waste products can build up and damage the cell.
 
• This can lead to a variety of diseases, including cancer and lysosomal storage diseases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribosome**:-

 
 
• ** A ribosome is a complex molecular machine that synthesizes proteins from amino acids. **
 
• It is found in all living cells, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic. Ribosomes are made up of two subunits, a large one and a small one.
 
• The small subunit binds to messenger RNA (mRNA) and decodes the genetic code, while the large subunit adds amino acids to the growing polypeptide chain.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**:-
 
 
• **Mitochondria, often referred to as the "powerhouses of the cell," are specialized organelles found in most eukaryotic organisms. **
 
• They are primarily responsible for energy production in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) through the process of oxidative phosphorylation.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles**:-
 
 
• **These are membrane-bound organelles present in all plant and fungal cells and some protist, animal and bacterial cells. **
 
• They're essentially enclosed compartments filled with water containing inorganic and organic molecules, including enzymes.

questions.question: Which membrane-bound cell organelle consisting of a small sac-like structure surrounded by single membranes serves as the cell's digestive system, allowing material taken from outside the cell to degrade and digest obsolete components of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lysosome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Lysosome:

 
 
• Lysosomes are an important cell organelle found within eukaryotic animal cells.
 
• Due to their peculiar function, they are also known as the “suicide bags” of the cell.
 
• Lysosomes work as the waste-discarding structures of the cell by processing undesirable materials and degrading them, both from the exterior of the cell and waste constituents inside the cell.
 
• But sometimes, the digestive enzymes may end up damaging the lysosomes themselves, and this can cause the cell to die.
 
• This is termed autolysis, where **“auto” means “self” and “lysis” means “the disintegration of the cell by the destruction of its cell membrane“**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is a microbody.
 
• In-plant it helps in photorespiration.
 
• In animals concerned with peroxide metabolism.
 
 
 
• Glyoxysomes: These are the **special type of peroxisomes found in plants & some fungi.**
 
• **Polysome:** Many **ribosomes may associate with a single mRNA** to form **multiple copies of a polypeptide simultaneously**.
 
 
• Such strings of ribosomes are termed as **Polysome**.

questions.question: ______ is the division of the cytoplasm of one eukaryotic cell into two daughter cells.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Cytokinesis.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The correct option is "Cytokinesis".**
 
• **Cytokinesis is the process by which the cytoplasm of a eukaryotic cell divides into two daughter cells after mitosis or meiosis.**
 
• During cytokinesis, a contractile ring made of actin and myosin filaments forms around the cell, which then contracts and divides the cytoplasm into two parts.
 
• ** In animal cells, cytokinesis** results in the formation of a cleavage furrow, while in plant cells, a cell plate forms in the middle of the cell and grows outward until it reaches the cell wall.
 
• **Cytokinesis is a crucial step in cell division,** as it ensures that each daughter cell receives a complete set of chromosomes and other cellular components necessary for survival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition caused by the body's response to an infection**. It has no relation to cytokinesis.
 
• **Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus of a eukaryotic **cell into two daughter nuclei during cell division. It is different from cytokinesis, which involves the division of the cytoplasm.
 
• **Genesis refers to the beginning or origin** of something and has no relation to cell division or cytokinesis.

options.text: Mitochondria and nucleus are found in bacteria.
Ribosomes, mitochondria and lysosomes are found in animal cells.
Chloroplast, ribosomes and nucleus are present in fungal cell.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes, mitochondria and lysosomes are found in animal cells.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes **are found in all cells, including animal cells.

 
 
• **Ribosomes are responsible for synthesizing proteins.**
 
 
 
• Mitochondria are the energy-producing organelles in animal cells.
 
 
• Mitochondria are organelles that are found in eukaryotic cells (cells that have a nucleus) and are responsible for producing energy in the form of ATP.
 
 
 
• Lysosomes are also found in animal cells and are responsible for breaking down waste materials.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **In fact, plant cells have additional organelles such as chloroplasts, cell walls, and** large central vacuoles** that are not found in animal cells.**
 
• Chloroplasts are organelles that are found in plant cells and are responsible for photosynthesis, the process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.
 
• **Fungal cells are eukaryotic cells that have a nucleus and organelles such as ribosomes and a nucleus.**
 
• They do not have chloroplasts, which are only found in plant cells.

questions.question:

I. It is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets.

questions.solution:

__
 
• Endoplasmic reticulum:

 
 
• The network or reticulum of tiny tubular structures scattered in the cytoplasm is called the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
 
• The ER divides the intracellular space into two distinct compartments, i.e., luminal (inside ER) and extraluminal (cytoplasm) compartments.
 
• The ER is of two types based on the presence or absence of ribosomes on its surface.
 
• The Endoplasmic reticulum bearing ribosomes on their surface is called Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) whereas in the absence of the ribosomes they appear smooth and are called Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER).​__
 
• The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (smooth ER) is a membranous organelle found in most eukaryotic cells. Its functions include 
 
• Synthesis of Lipids, including cholesterol and phospholipids.
 
• Steroid Hormones.
 
• Storage and metabolism of calcium ions within the cell.
 
• Detoxification of harmful metabolic byproducts/toxic substances.
 
• Glycogenolysis i.e the breakdown of the molecule glycogen into glucose.

• Plasm a membrane, also called the cell membrane is mainly composed of lipids and proteins.
 
• The major lipids are arranged in a bilayer and are called phospholipids.
 
• The plasma membrane also contains cholesterol.
 
• Cell membranes also possess protein and carbohydrates as per Biochemical investigation.
 
• The ratio of lipids and proteins varies in different cell types.
 
• For example, in human beings, the membrane of the erythrocyte has approx 40 per cent lipids and 52 per cent protein.

questions.question: Which of the following cell divisions is known as reduction division?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis**:-

 
 
• **It is known as reduction division because it reduces the number of chromosomes in a cell by half, resulting in four haploid daughter cells.**
 
• This process is essential for sexual reproduction as it allows for the formation of gametes with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell, which then combine during fertilization to form a zygote with a full set of chromosomes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telophase:-**

 
 
• It is a stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the nuclear membrane reforms around the separated chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
 
 
 
• **Prophase:-**
 
 
• It is the stage in both mitosis and meiosis where the chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, but it is not known as reduction division.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis:-**
 
 
• It is a type of cell division where a single cell divides into two identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It does not involve a reduction in chromosome number and is not known as reduction division.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is an overlapping membranous sac with ER-like thickness that helps in processing and packaging protein and lipid molecules, especially stable proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golgi apparatus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Golgi Apparatus:**__

__
 
• The Golgi apparatus has multiple names such as the **Golgi complex or Golgi body.**
 
• The name is given on the name of the scientist, who discovered the organelle, i.e. Camillo Golgi.
 
• It is **found in all the eukaryotic cells**, plants as well as animals.
 
• They are membrane-bound organelles present in the cytosol of the cell.
 
• The Golgi body comprises 5 to 8 cup-shaped, series of compartments known as **cisternae**. Cisternae is a flattened, disk-shaped, stacked pouches that make up the Golgi apparatus. A Golgi stack mostly contains 4 to 8 cisternae. However, ~60 cisternae are found in some protists. A mammalian cell contains ~40 to 100 stacks of cisternae.
 
• Animal cells generally contain around 10 to 20 Golgi stacks per cell, which are connected by tubular connections.
 
• Golgi complex is mostly found near the nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a66665c8b7d6a84497438e44c0511f463d9d862ee49c9ea1be606ed25af9562.png] 

**Functions of Golgi Bodies:**__

 
• Its main function is the **packaging and secretion of proteins.** 
 
• It receives proteins from Endoplasmic Reticulum. It packages it into **membrane-bound vesicles**, which are then transported to various destinations, such as lysosomes, plasma membrane or secretion.
 
• They also take part in the** transport of lipids **and the formation of lysosomes.
 
• **Post-translational modification and enzymatic processing** occur near the membrane surface in Golgi bodies, e.g. phosphorylation, glycosylation, etc.
 
• Golgi apparatus is the site for the synthesis of various glycolipids, sphingomyelin, etc.
 
• In the plant cells,** complex polysaccharides of the cell wall** are synthesised in the Golgi apparatus.

questions.question: What are the thin filamentous extensions that the motile bacterial cells have from their cell wall called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flagella**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The thin filamentous extensions that motile bacterial cells have from their cell wall are called **Flagella**.
 
• Flagella are lash-like appendages that protrude from the cell body of certain prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, providing the means for locomotion.
 
• They are essential for the motility of bacteria, allowing them to move toward favorable environments or away from harmful ones.
 
• Flagella are composed of the protein flagellin and are powered by a rotary engine at the base of the flagellum.
 
• They are different from other cell appendages like pili and fimbriae, which are primarily involved in attachment rather than movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In the context of movement of cells, exocytosis is the process by which:

• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found in animal cells.
 
• They contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down biomolecules, including proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids.
 
• They are often referred to as the "digestive system" of the cell due to their role in breaking down cellular waste and debris.
 
• Lysosomes are essential for cellular homeostasis, recycling cellular components through a process known as autophagy.

• It helps maintain cellular health by removing damaged organelles and misfolded proteins.
 
• It plays a crucial role in cellular responses to stress and starvation.
 
 
 
• **Enzymatic Function:**
 
 
• Lysosomal enzymes are acidic hydrolases that function optimally at acidic pH.
 
• The acidic environment inside lysosomes is maintained by proton pumps in the lysosomal membrane.

• Examples include Tay-Sachs disease, Gaucher's disease, and Pompe disease.

• Lysosomes play a role in the immune response by digesting pathogens engulfed by phagocytic cells.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following about mitosis.

options.text: Each cell called mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells.
It helps in growth and repair of tissues in organisms.
The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as mother cell.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The daughter cells have half the number of chromosomes as mother cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mitosis is a type of **cell division** that results in two genetically identical daughter cells from a single parent cell.
 
• The daughter cells produced by mitosis have the **same number of chromosomes** as the parent cell, making them diploid.
 
• This process is essential for the **growth, repair, and maintenance** of tissues in multicellular organisms.
 
• Unlike meiosis, which results in daughter cells with half the number of chromosomes (haploid), mitosis maintains the **chromosome number** of the original cell.
 
• Mitosis consists of several phases: **Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase, and Cytokinesis**, ensuring accurate chromosome segregation and cell division.
 
• The incorrect statement suggests that mitosis results in daughter cells with half the chromosomes, which is characteristic of **meiosis**, not mitosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Each cell called mother cell divides to form two identical daughter cells**__

 __
 
• This is a correct statement as mitosis results in the formation of **two genetically identical daughter cells** from a single parent cell.
 
• It ensures that the daughter cells maintain the **same genetic makeup** as the parent cell.
 
 
 
• **It helps in growth and repair of tissues in organisms**__
 __
 
• Mitosis plays a crucial role in **growth, development, and repair** of tissues in multicellular organisms.
 
• It is vital for the replacement of damaged or dead cells, ensuring the proper functioning of tissues and organs.
 
 
 
• **Cells divide for growth**__
 
 
• Mitosis is a fundamental process for **cellular growth** and development, allowing organisms to increase in size.
 
• This division ensures that new cells are available for the expansion and maintenance of tissues.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles possesses their own DNA and can synthesise protein for their functions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroplast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chloroplasts** are organelles found in plant cells and eukaryotic algae that conduct photosynthesis.
 
• They have their own **DNA and ribosomes**, similar to mitochondria, which allows them to synthesize proteins independently.
 
• The DNA present in chloroplasts is **circular** and resembles the DNA of prokaryotes.
 
• Chloroplasts are known for containing the pigment **chlorophyll**, which is essential for capturing light energy.
 
• They play a crucial role in converting light energy into chemical energy through the process of **photosynthesis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endosymbiotic Theory**

 
 
• This theory suggests that chloroplasts and mitochondria were once free-living prokaryotes.
 
• They were engulfed by a host cell and developed a symbiotic relationship.
 
• This theory is supported by the presence of their own DNA and double membranes.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis Process**
 
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in two stages: the light-dependent reactions and the Calvin cycle.
 
• In the light-dependent reactions, energy from light is used to produce ATP and NADPH.
 
• In the Calvin cycle, ATP and NADPH are used to convert carbon dioxide into glucose.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Chloroplast**
 
 
• Chloroplasts have an outer membrane, an inner membrane, and a thylakoid membrane system.
 
• The thylakoid membranes contain chlorophyll and are the site of the light-dependent reactions.
 
• The stroma is the fluid-filled space surrounding the thylakoids where the Calvin cycle takes place.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Engineering**
 
 
• Chloroplast DNA can be used in genetic engineering to introduce new traits in plants.
 
• Transgenic plants with modified chloroplast genomes can produce biofuels, pharmaceuticals, and other valuable products.
 
• Research in this area is ongoing to enhance the efficiency of photosynthesis and crop yields.

questions.question: In 1873, who published the first photograph of nerve tissue stained with the black reaction technique, describing a whole nerve cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Camillo Golgi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Camillo Golgi** developed the black reaction technique (also known as Golgi's method) in 1873, which was a major advancement in neuroanatomy.
 
• This staining technique made it possible to visualize the detailed structure and organization of nerve cells and their intricate networks.
 
• The black reaction involves using silver chromate to stain a few cells in their entirety, allowing for the observation of individual neurons against a transparent background.
 
• This method was instrumental in establishing the neuron doctrine, which states that the neuron is the basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system.
 
• Golgi shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1906 with Santiago Ramón y Cajal for their work on the structure of the nervous system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Golgi apparatus**, an important cellular organelle involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles, was also discovered by Camillo Golgi.
 
• Golgi's contributions to cell biology and neuroscience are foundational, with the Golgi method continuing to influence neuroscientific research well into the 20th century and beyond.
 
• His work laid the groundwork for understanding the complex connectivity and functions of the nervous system, influencing both basic science and clinical approaches to neurological diseases.
 
• The Golgi method's ability to selectively stain neurons is still appreciated for its utility in highlighting the intricate details of cell morphology and connectivity.
